comparison: Perfect agreement on C1, C8-C10. Both evaluations find the molecular marker identification (Cdh6/Cdh8) and expression patterns well-supported by RNAscope data. Peer reviewers praised the work as 'important' and 'impressive,' while OpenEval noted appropriate sample sizes and statistical measures.

Strong agreement on C11-C20, C67 regarding marker colocalization and regional differences. Both evaluations accept the comprehensive RNAscope data without challenge. Peer reviewers noted the data 'increases information regarding the properties of IPANs in mice' and OpenEval confirmed appropriate quantification and statistical significance.

Complete agreement on C3, C41-C43 regarding morphological characterization. Both evaluations accept the biocytin-filled neuron tracings and morphological classifications. Peer reviewers praised 'state-of-the-art physiological setups' and OpenEval noted consistency with established IPAN features.

Agreement on C24-C36 electrophysiological characterization, though with different emphases. OpenEval noted small sample size (N=5) as a limitation while still supporting the claims. Peer reviewers accepted the findings as part of comprehensive approach, with one noting scope limitation to distal colon rather than challenging validity. Peer review also includes C4-C5, C37-C40 not in OpenEval R4.

Partial overlap on C37-C40 regarding voltage clamp identification of IH and IT. OpenEval R5 supports these claims based on technical advances, while peer R4 accepts electrophysiological characterization broadly. Both note the work is limited to specific neuronal populations.

Agreement on C21-C23 regarding Hb9:GFP model validation. Both evaluations accept the sparse labeling strategy without challenge. OpenEval notes validation via RNAscope and prior citations, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the comprehensive genetic model approach. OpenEval also includes C130 not addressed in peer R8.

Divergent evaluations on C44-C49 regarding tdTomato expression patterns. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while acknowledging off-target labeling in muscle cells as a noted limitation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising significant concerns about off-target expression and requesting better characterization and control experiments, though authors later provided additional discussion.

Divergent evaluations on C6, C50-C56, C59, C76 regarding optogenetic experiments. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and statistical analysis. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting critical controls for ChR2 expression effects, stimulation intensity validation, and regional response comparability. However, editor noted many controls were provided in prior publications and the multi-technique approach is compelling.

Partial overlap on C57-C58 regarding hexamethonium experiments. OpenEval R9 supports these pharmacological findings (also C84-C85), while peer R5 addresses broader optogenetic concerns. The hexamethonium data itself was not challenged by peer reviewers.

Agreement on C84-C85 regarding nicotinic cholinergic transmission role in CMCs. Both evaluations accept the hexamethonium experiments demonstrating that optogenetically-evoked CMCs require the same cholinergic circuitry as spontaneous CMCs.

Agreement on C7, C60-C66, C94 regarding IH blocker effects on CMCs. Both evaluations support the pharmacological findings with ZD7288. OpenEval notes marginally non-significant p-value for one effect. Peer reviewers accepted the data while noting that blocking IH affects all IPANs (specificity limitation rather than validity challenge).

Complete agreement on C68-C70 regarding Cdh9 versus Cdh6/Cdh8 expression patterns. Both evaluations accept the comparative findings about different cadherin-expressing IPAN populations based on RNA-Seq data and prior literature without challenge.

Agreement on uncertainty for C100-C111 regarding Cdh6 synaptic function. Both evaluations note speculation about synaptic roles lacks direct evidence. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to failure to detect Cdh6 protein via immunohistochemistry. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, noting Cdh6 has non-synaptic functions and requesting immunostaining validation, though authors later provided additional discussion.

Agreement on uncertainty for C77-C80 regarding regional difference mechanisms. Both evaluations note these are speculative explanations lacking direct experimental support. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting observations are well-documented but mechanisms require further investigation. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning why regional differences exist and requesting better characterization. Peer R11 also includes C81-C83.

Partial overlap on C81-C83 providing context about prior IPAN work. OpenEval R16 supports these as accurate literature summaries. Peer R11 addresses these in context of uncertainty about regional differences (C77-C80), using prior literature to frame questions about mechanisms.

Divergent evaluations on C88-C89, C95-C99 regarding IH mechanistic interpretations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about rhythmicity mechanisms (single neuron vs network) lacks direct evidence despite reasonable analogies. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the identification of IH/IT and pharmacological demonstration of IH's role without challenging mechanistic interpretations. Peer R13 also includes C86-C87, C90-C93.

Partial overlap on C90-C93 regarding functional context for IH. OpenEval R14 supports these as appropriate citations to prior work providing important context. Peer R13 accepts the broader electrophysiological characterization including these contextual claims as part of the comprehensive approach.

Agreement on C112-C129 as supported background/contextual claims. Both evaluations accept these literature-based claims providing scientific foundation and rationale. OpenEval notes appropriate citations to established literature. Peer reviewers did not challenge these, though one noted some findings confirm known characteristics from other species. Peer R15 also includes C72-C75, C130.

Partial overlap on C72-C75 summarizing prior IPAN work. OpenEval R16 supports these as accurate literature summaries with appropriate citations. Peer R15 accepts these contextual claims while noting some findings confirm established knowledge from other species.

Minimal overlap on C130 regarding sparse labeling. OpenEval R3 includes this as part of validation for the genetic model approach. Peer R15 addresses this in broader context of background claims and study rationale.

Peer reviewers noted scope limitation regarding C71 (submucosal plexus IPANs not included in Cdh6 analysis). This limitation was acknowledged rather than challenging validity of findings. No corresponding OpenEval result addresses this specific scope limitation.
